title: Veridian Systems - Hybrid Marketplace Connector Compatibility Check-in
summary: Follow-up technical sync focused on Veridian's marketplace listing and the hybrid (VPC/on-prem) connector. Reviewed helm packaging, auth integration (SAML/SSO), KMS/HSM compatibility, and a proposed fallback routing pattern for constrained edge sites. Agreed to run an end-to-end UAT in staging with a smoke benchmark and provide packaging notes for Microsoft/AWS marketplaces.
topics: Helm chart and operator differences for Veridian private clusters
SAML and SCIM provisioning for marketplace flows
KMS/HSM key wrapping and customer-managed keys
Routing and fallback for low-bandwidth edge sites
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Elliot Tan (Redwood Product), Samira Lopez (Redwood Solutions), Carlos Ruiz (Veridian CTO), Maya Chen (Veridian SRE), Jordan Bell (Platform Eng), Lina Park (Security)

Auto-summary: quick tech run-through; action items captured at end.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Thursday afternoon, appreciate it. I'll hand it over to Priya to kick us off with the integration checklist.
[00:18] Priya (SE): Hi all, yes thanks. Quick agenda — helm/operator packaging, auth and identity, network connectivity (VPC & on-prem tunnel), KMS/HSM, and then a proposed fallback routing for low bandwidth sites. We want to validate the marketplace artifacts and land a staging UAT.
[00:40] Carlos (CTO): Sounds good. For context, our primary ask is that Veridian's managed appliance can pull from the marketplace listing but also talk to Redwood private endpoints inside our VPC without exposing data. So basically hybrid.
[01:05] Maya (SRE): And we run a mix of EKS and a few on prem kube clusters with restricted egress. Some sites only have 3–4 Mbps, so latency and fallback are real concerns.
[01:32] Priya (SE): Got it. On the helm side — we recommend packaging both a simple helm chart and an operator-based installation. The chart will be used by marketplace installers; the operator handles lifecycle if you want automated upgrades.
[01:50] Jordan (Platform Eng): Quick question — do you require our clusters to have outbound to Redwood's public API, or is there an option for a VPC connector? We can't open wide egress at some of our customer edge networks.
[02:10] Alex (AE): There are two paths — a VPC connector (private peering) for Dedicated/Private installs, or a relay tunnel client that lives locally and tunnels via an approved egress to a regional gateway. Both are supported; Priya can share the network flow diagrams.
[02:36] Priya (SE): Yeah I'll share the diagrams. For the tunnel client we use a persistent TLS stream and optional proxying — that pattern works for constrained egress. We do prefix caching on request side to reduce calls. Note: the auto cache may be mis-transcribed — it's prefix K V cache, works at token level.
[03:05] Lina (Security): On keys — our security team requires BYOK with HSM-backed key wrapping. Can Redwood support a customer-managed KMS key and an HSM attestation?
[03:22] Elliot (Product): Short answer yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (we've done KMS integrations with AWS & Azure), and HSM attestation is supported for on-prem HSMs with key wrapping. We will need the KMS ARN and the attestation artifacts.
[03:45] Carlos (CTO): And what about audit logs? We need request-level logs, but they must not contain customer PII. Is there a redaction step?
[04:02] Samira (Solutions): We provide structured audit logs with token-level metadata only. We can toggle redaction settings — we usually send pseudo tokens and metadata, not raw inputs unless you enable verbose auditing. We'll share our audit-format doc.
[04:20] Jordan (Eng): Great. Back to helm — are there any marketplace-specific requirements for images, SBOMs, or attestations for MS/AWS marketplaces? We need to line those up.
[04:36] Priya (SE): Yes — images must be signed, include SBOM, and you need attestations for vulnerability scanning. Redwood can produce a build manifest to help. We'll attach a marketplace checklist that matches both Azure and AWS.
[04:55] Maya (SRE): For the cluster connector, what's the recommended liveness/readiness pattern? We had issues with KV cache warmup causing liveness to fail in the first minute during heavy startup.
[05:15] Priya (SE): Recommend a longer initial grace period for liveness at install time — 3 minutes — and readiness gating until KV cache warms. Also use a small startup-replica of 1 to prime caches before scaling to desired replicas. We'll document a helm values snippet.
[05:40] Carlos: If a regional Redwood capacity outage happens, what fallback options exist? We can't afford hard failures.
[05:55] Alex: You can set policy routes: fallback to a lower-tier model hosted locally, or route to another region. For on-prem we can pin a quantized model to the private runtime as last resort. This is part of the graceful degradation pattern.
[06:20] Maya: Is model pinning available in the operator?
[06:28] Priya: Yes, via the operator you can pin model versions and provide a local model bundle in k8s volume. The operator will prefer local bundles if network connectivity is missing.
[06:45] Jordan: Ok makes sense. Let's dig into SAML. Do you support SP-initiated or IdP-initiated flows for marketplace SSO?
[06:58] Elliot: We support both. For marketplace installs we usually do SP-initiated for the admin console, but the operator supports SCIM for provisioning. We'll coordinate attribute mapping.
[07:18] Lina: SCIM — we need to ensure group mappings and least privilege roles. Can we map groups to RBAC roles at install?
[07:30] Priya: Yes, the operator supports role mapping config, we'll share an example.
[07:40] Carlos: On the marketplace side, certification will require us to submit SBOM and a security questionnaire. Can Redwood provide a prefilled security questionnaire about your runtime and data handling?
[07:55] Samira: Absolutely. We'll send the security questionnaire and the SOC2 artifacts redacted. We'll also include our dataflow diagrams for the marketplace listing.
[08:15] Maya: For the KMS integration, how do you handle key rotation without downtime? We rotate keys quarterly.
[08:26] Priya: We support key rotation via double-wrapping: new keys are staged and both old and new keys are accepted during transition window. The operator will reload KMS config without restart for most cases. We'll share rotation playbook.
[08:45] Jordan: Performance — we want to run a short smoke benchmark. What metrics do you recommend? Latency p50/p95, tokens/s, and CPU/GPU utilization?
[08:59] Alex: Yep, p50/p95, end-to-end latency, and cost tokens per second. For the smoke we'll provide a small load harness that runs on your staging cluster and pushes through the VPC or tunnel. Expect about 20–30 minutes to set up.
[09:20] Carlos: Ok. Regarding packaging for marketplaces, do we need an operator or just helm? Some customers prefer operator for automated upgrades but marketplace sandbox expects a simple helm install.
[09:35] Samira: We suggest publishing both — helm for marketplace quick installs and operator for customers who want lifecycle management. The operator can be offered as an optional marketplace addon.
[09:50] Maya: A random edge case — some of our clients use FIPS-enabled kernels. Does Redwood support FIPS-compliant crypto for the tunnel and KMS calls?
[10:04] Priya: We have a FIPS-compliant build path for the tunnel client and TLS stacks; it's an advanced binary build. We'll note the steps and limitations — e.g. some third-party libs may not be FIPS-validated.
[10:25] Jordan: Cool. Can we talk about image sizes? Marketplace has a limit for uncompressed image layers for cold nodes in some regions. Our on-prem nodes have limited disk.
[10:37] Elliot: We recommend slim images and multi-arch manifests. For operator-managed images we support layering so large models are mounted as volumes rather than in the container image. That keeps image size small.
[10:57] Alex: Also for model artifacts we can provide delta downloads or chunked pulls to reduce disk footprint.
[11:10] Carlos: Any known gotchas for the Azure marketplace specifically?
[11:18] Samira: Azure requires attestation for ACIs and a validated SBOM. We'll include a checklist. Also image signing policy is stricter — you'll need sigstore or equivalent.
[11:35] Maya: On deployment orchestration — when operator upgrades happen, how do we avoid rolling restarts that disrupt the KV cache?
[11:48] Priya: Use a zero-downtime rollout strategy: do not restart priming replica; cordon and drain gracefully, use preStop hooks to persist KV state to a local PVC. We'll provide hooks sample.
[12:05] Jordan: All right we should put some dates on the UAT. We're targeting a marketplace submission by end of Q2. That gives us roughly 12 weeks.
[12:17] Alex: Good. For that timeline, recommended milestones: packaging and SBOM (2 weeks), security questionnaire (1–2 weeks), staging UAT & smoke (3 weeks), marketplace certification queue (variable).
[12:36] Carlos: Let's plan for a short benchmark next week. We'll schedule time with your SRE.
[12:45] Priya: Perfect. On the fallback routing you mentioned — can you sketch how a site with 3 Mbps would behave?
[12:55] Alex: Sure — primary path: call Redwood hosted inference via VPC connector. If the p95 latency exceeds threshold or bandwidth fall below X, fallback: (1) route requests to local pinned, quantized model on operator; (2) if local not available, degrade model size or batch tokens and return a shorter completion; (3) emit alert and throttle non-critical requests.
[13:25] Maya: That approach sounds reasonable. We want a deterministic behavior.
[13:33] Priya: We'll codify the policy in the operator config as routingPolicies.
[13:40] Jordan: Ok. Now let's surface the open integration tasks.
[13:46] Carlos: For Security, Lina will handle the questionnaire and HSM attestation requirements.
[13:51] Lina: Yes. I'll need the KMS playbook and a sample attestation template.
[13:58] Samira: We'll send both.
[14:02] Priya: For the helm values, we'll create a minimal example and an operator values example.
[14:10] Elliot: I'll prepare the marketplace SBOM template and sign tool recommendations.
[14:16] Jordan: We'll prepare a staging cluster and allocate a VPN endpoint for the tunnel client.
[14:22] Alex: Great. Any blockers we should know about?
[14:26] Carlos: Only internal headcount to run the UAT, but we can commit a platform eng and SRE.
[14:35] Maya: Also need clarity on disk usage for pinned models — we'll take the numbers you provide and size PVCs.
[14:42] Priya: We'll include model bundle sizes and recommended PVC sizes per model profile.
[14:50] Alex: Ok let's run through quick Q&A. Carlos?
[14:54] Carlos: For the marketplace certification, do you support automated vulnerability scans or do we need to run our 3rd party scanning before submission?
[15:05] Samira: Redwood will run a baseline scan, but customers must provide their scans for legal listings. We can accept your SCA/VA reports.
[15:16] Lina: For audit retention policies, can we set retention to 90 days and then export to our SIEM?
[15:24] Elliot: Yes, retention is configurable and we support streaming logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders.
[15:33] Jordan: On the operator side, does it auto-upgrade minor versions by default?
[15:39] Priya: No, default is manual approval; we can enable auto minor upgrades via canary if you choose.
[15:48] Carlos: Anything else on encryption in transit? We need mTLS between the operator and Redwood endpoints in private mode.
[15:56] Priya: mTLS is supported — the operator will present a client cert signed by the customer's CA or Redwood CA depending on settings. We'll provide the cert workflow.
[16:07] Maya: For the staging UAT, can you provide a quickstart script that seeds the model cache with a small prompt set?
[16:17] Alex: Yes we'll include a seeding harness and a smoke script.
[16:23] Priya: We'll also include a Prometheus metrics list you can scrape for p50/p95.
[16:30] Jordan: Okay that helps.
[16:33] Carlos: Last thing — any competitor behaviors we should watch for? We're talking to two others (ObsidianAI and CloudForge) about marketplace flows. Anything unique on Redwood's side we should push in discussions?
[16:49] Alex: Two things — unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private (so same API surface) and the cost-aware batching controls. Those are differentiators. We'll send a short one-pager.
[17:05] Priya: Also our KV cache warmup and model pinning options for offline sites are often highlighted.
[17:12] Maya: Great.
[17:18] Alex: All right let's capture action items.
